scr_cash_introduction_to_cash_management.purpose: Introduces Cash Management — the RealPage application for bank accounts, deposits, funds transfers, manual and electronic payments, other receipts, available cash, positive pay, escheatment and bank reconciliation for every property bank account.
scr_cash_introduction_to_cash_management.outcome: Accountants understand that every movement of property cash that is not a routine A/P check or A/R receipt is recorded and reconciled here.
scr_cash_introduction_to_cash_management.rootCause: Multifamily properties hold several restricted and unrestricted accounts (operating, security deposit trust, payroll, reserves). Cash is the asset most exposed to fraud and the one owners check first, so a dedicated application controls its setup, movement and reconciliation.
scr_cash_introduction_to_cash_management.ifSkipped: Cash activity is recorded inconsistently across modules, bank recs break, and restricted cash is mixed with operating cash.
redFlags: Cash movements recorded as manual JEs instead of Cash Management transactions

scr_cash_cash_management_home_page.purpose: The Cash Management home page with icon navigation to bank accounts, deposits, transfers, electronic payments, available cash and reconciliation.
scr_cash_cash_management_home_page.outcome: Quick access to the daily and monthly cash tasks from one landing page.
scr_cash_cash_management_home_page.rootCause: Cash tasks are frequent and time-sensitive (daily deposits, payment file uploads before bank cut-off). A task-oriented home page reduces the chance of missing a cut-off.
scr_cash_cash_management_home_page.ifSkipped: Users hunt through menus and miss bank cut-off times for ACH and positive pay files.
gaap: NACHA operating rules — file submission windows
redFlags: Payment files uploaded after the bank's same-day cut-off

scr_cash_cash_management_all_tab.purpose: The All tab of Cash Management listing Search & Find (bank and credit card accounts), Periodic Tasks (deposits, transfers, manual payments, other receipts, available cash, payment files, positive pay, reconciliation) and Reports.
scr_cash_cash_management_all_tab.outcome: All operational cash functions are reachable in one tab.
scr_cash_cash_management_all_tab.rootCause: Cash work is a daily routine with many small tasks; grouping them keeps the routine consistent across properties.
scr_cash_cash_management_all_tab.ifSkipped: Some routine cash tasks are forgotten, especially positive pay and payment confirmations.
redFlags: Positive pay not in the daily routine

scr_cash_cash_management_setup_tab.purpose: The Setup tab where Cash Management configuration lives — escheatment account, holdback names, available cash fields, reconciliation permissions and electronic payment settings.
scr_cash_cash_management_setup_tab.outcome: Cash processes behave according to company policy (e.g., which account escheated funds go to, which holdbacks reduce available cash).
scr_cash_cash_management_setup_tab.rootCause: Settings like the escheatment liability account and holdback definitions determine how cash is reported to owners; they must be configured deliberately by administrators.
scr_cash_cash_management_setup_tab.ifSkipped: Escheated items post to the wrong account and available cash overstates what can be distributed.
redFlags: No escheatment account configured while escheatment workbench is in use

scr_cash_using_cash_management.purpose: Overview of the operational tasks in Cash Management — escheatment, bank and card accounts, deposits, transfers, manual payments, receipts, available cash, electronic payments, positive pay and reconciliations.
scr_cash_using_cash_management.outcome: A map of which cash task solves which operational need.
scr_cash_using_cash_management.rootCause: Bank recs are the most frequent month-end finding; most rec breaks trace back to cash activity recorded in the wrong place. Knowing the right tool for each cash event prevents them.
scr_cash_using_cash_management.ifSkipped: Cash events recorded via JEs or wrong screens, leaving the bank rec unmatched.
redFlags: High volume of unmatched bank lines every month

scr_cash_escheatment_workbench_page.purpose: The workbench page listing uncashed items by escheatment stage — outstanding, aged payable, due for escheat, escheated — with filters and actions to move items through the process.
scr_cash_escheatment_workbench_page.outcome: A single queue of stale checks and credits that must be resolved under state unclaimed property rules.
scr_cash_escheatment_workbench_page.rootCause: Stale items sit in outstanding-check lists across dozens of bank accounts. Without a consolidated queue, due-diligence deadlines and state reporting dates (often November 1 or March 1) are missed.
scr_cash_escheatment_workbench_page.ifSkipped: State reports are late or incomplete, exposing the company to penalties and interest in unclaimed property audits.
gaap: ASC 405-20 — liabilities not extinguished by aging
redFlags: Items past dormancy with no due-diligence letter
Resident refund checks older than state dormancy

scr_cash_filtering_the_escheatment_workb.purpose: Filters the escheatment workbench by item type (four types, such as outstanding checks and aged payables), property, state and age to focus on items approaching each state's dormancy period.
scr_cash_filtering_the_escheatment_workb.outcome: The accountant works items by state deadline rather than scrolling the whole portfolio.
scr_cash_filtering_the_escheatment_workb.rootCause: Dormancy periods and report dates differ by state (e.g., 3 years for most property in many states, shorter for wages). Filtering by state and age is how compliance teams meet each state's cycle.
scr_cash_filtering_the_escheatment_workb.ifSkipped: Items for states with earlier deadlines are missed while effort goes to others.
gaap: State-specific dormancy periods and reporting deadlines
redFlags: No filter by owner's last-known-address state (priority rule)

scr_cash_marking_an_invoice_as_an_aged_p.purpose: Moves an uncashed payment back to a liability — the check is voided in cash and the obligation is recorded as an aged payable — so the bank rec no longer carries it as outstanding while the owed amount remains a liability until claimed or escheated.
scr_cash_marking_an_invoice_as_an_aged_p.outcome: Stale checks leave the bank reconciliation, and the money owed stays correctly recorded as a liability.
scr_cash_marking_an_invoice_as_an_aged_p.rootCause: Stale outstanding checks clutter bank recs, but voiding them to income or expense is an escheat violation. Converting them to aged payables keeps the liability while cleaning the rec.
scr_cash_marking_an_invoice_as_an_aged_p.ifSkipped: Either the rec carries years of stale items, or accountants void them to income, creating unclaimed property exposure.
redFlags: Stale checks voided without being converted to aged payables

scr_cash_configuring_an_escheatment_acco.purpose: Sets up the GL account used when aged payables are escheated — typically a liability such as Unclaimed Property Payable — in Cash Management configuration.
scr_cash_configuring_an_escheatment_acco.outcome: Escheated amounts post consistently to a dedicated liability until remitted to the state.
scr_cash_configuring_an_escheatment_acco.rootCause: Escheat postings need a controlled liability account so the amount due to states can be reconciled to state reports and remittances.
scr_cash_configuring_an_escheatment_acco.ifSkipped: Escheated items post to miscellaneous accounts and state remittances cannot be reconciled.
redFlags: Escheat account set to an income account

scr_cash_reverting_an_aged_payable_to_a_.purpose: Reverses an aged payable back to its original posted or paid state — used when the payee finally cashes the check, or the item was aged in error.
scr_cash_reverting_an_aged_payable_to_a_.outcome: The payment status and cash position reflect that the payee has claimed the funds.
scr_cash_reverting_an_aged_payable_to_a_.rootCause: Payees sometimes deposit old checks or contact the property after items are aged. The system must restore the original transaction rather than creating a second payment.
scr_cash_reverting_an_aged_payable_to_a_.ifSkipped: Duplicate payments are issued or bank recs break when an old check clears.
redFlags: Reissued payment while the original check is still negotiable

scr_cash_including_aged_invoices_in_the_.purpose: Option in the Vendor Aging report to include aged payables so the A/P aging reflects stale obligations moved out of cash.
scr_cash_including_aged_invoices_in_the_.outcome: The A/P aging agrees with the GL when aged payables sit in the A/P or unclaimed property accounts.
scr_cash_including_aged_invoices_in_the_.rootCause: Aged payables are still liabilities. Excluding them from the aging makes the A/P tie-out fail or hides the liability from reviewers.
scr_cash_including_aged_invoices_in_the_.ifSkipped: A/P subledger and GL don't tie, or stale liabilities are invisible in the aging.
redFlags: Aging run without aged items while GL includes them

scr_cash_marking_an_aged_payable_as_esch.purpose: After funds are remitted to the state, marks the aged payable as escheated, clearing it from the liability and recording the remittance.
scr_cash_marking_an_aged_payable_as_esch.outcome: The liability is extinguished only when the state has received the funds, with a record of the remittance.
scr_cash_marking_an_aged_payable_as_esch.rootCause: Holders are released from liability when they remit to the state. Marking items escheated at that point keeps the books aligned with the state filing.
scr_cash_marking_an_aged_payable_as_esch.ifSkipped: Liabilities remain after remittance, or are cleared without remittance.
gaap: State unclaimed property laws — holder release on remittance
redFlags: Items marked escheated with no remittance evidence

scr_cash_exporting_transactions_from_the.purpose: Exports workbench items for due-diligence mailings and preparation of state unclaimed property reports (often in NAUPA format).
scr_cash_exporting_transactions_from_the.outcome: Data for due-diligence letters and state filings, pulled directly from the workbench.
scr_cash_exporting_transactions_from_the.rootCause: States require holder reports with owner name, last address, amount and dates. Exporting from the system avoids re-keying and omissions.
scr_cash_exporting_transactions_from_the.ifSkipped: State reports are compiled manually with missing items.
redFlags: Exports missing last-known addresses

scr_cash_search_and_find.purpose: Search & Find menus for bank accounts and credit card accounts — the master records every cash transaction references.
scr_cash_search_and_find.outcome: Accountants locate and maintain the account records behind cash activity.
scr_cash_search_and_find.rootCause: Bank and card account master data (GL mapping, restrictions, check numbering) drives how every payment and receipt posts; it needs a controlled maintenance point.
scr_cash_search_and_find.ifSkipped: Account master data errors propagate into every transaction.
redFlags: Accounts with outdated GL mappings

scr_cash_bank_accounts_list.purpose: Lists all company bank accounts — operating, security deposit trust, payroll, reserve, money market — with their GL cash accounts and entities, for viewing and maintenance.
scr_cash_bank_accounts_list.outcome: A complete inventory of bank accounts mapped to GL accounts and entities.
scr_cash_bank_accounts_list.rootCause: Every bank account must be reconciled monthly and mapped to the correct entity. An inventory ensures no account is left unreconciled and none is mapped to the wrong owner.
scr_cash_bank_accounts_list.ifSkipped: Accounts opened at the bank are never set up or reconciled, a common way fraud and errors go undetected.
redFlags: Bank accounts in the list with no reconciliation for recent months
Bank statements received for accounts not in the list

scr_cash_adding_a_bank_account.purpose: Sets up a new bank account — bank, routing and account number, GL cash account, entity, check numbering, and electronic payment settings — typically when a property is acquired or a new trust or reserve account is opened.
scr_cash_adding_a_bank_account.outcome: The account can be used for payments and deposits and reconciled from its first month.
scr_cash_adding_a_bank_account.rootCause: New acquisitions and new lender-required accounts must be set up before any activity; incorrect GL mapping here misstates cash for every future transaction.
scr_cash_adding_a_bank_account.ifSkipped: Activity in the new account is recorded elsewhere or not at all, and its first reconciliation fails.
gaap: State trust account requirements for security deposits
redFlags: Security deposit trust account mapped to the operating cash GL

scr_cash_adding_a_private_entity_level_b.purpose: Designates a bank account as private to one entity so only that entity's invoices can be paid from it — used for owner-specific operating and trust accounts.
scr_cash_adding_a_private_entity_level_b.outcome: One owner's cash cannot be used to pay another owner's bills.
scr_cash_adding_a_private_entity_level_b.rootCause: Management companies hold accounts for many owners. Paying one owner's invoice from another's account is a fiduciary breach and creates intercompany balances between unrelated owners.
scr_cash_adding_a_private_entity_level_b.ifSkipped: Cross-owner payments occur, requiring reimbursement and damaging owner trust.
redFlags: Owner accounts left unrestricted

scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_bank_accou.purpose: Opens a bank account record to review or update details — GL mapping, check numbers, electronic payment settings, restrictions.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_bank_accou.outcome: Bank account setup stays accurate as banking relationships change.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_bank_accou.rootCause: Banks change routing numbers after mergers, check stock is reordered, and positive pay settings change. Edits must be controlled because they affect where payments draw from.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_bank_accou.ifSkipped: Payments fail or draw from the wrong account after bank changes.
gaap: COSO 2013 — change controls over bank master data
redFlags: Bank detail changes without dual approval

scr_cash_deleting_a_bank_account.purpose: Deletes a bank account record that has no activity — typically one set up in error. Closed accounts with history should be inactivated, not deleted.
scr_cash_deleting_a_bank_account.outcome: Erroneous records removed without losing history of real accounts.
scr_cash_deleting_a_bank_account.rootCause: Deleting accounts with history would remove the audit trail of cash activity; deletion is only safe for unused records.
scr_cash_deleting_a_bank_account.ifSkipped: Duplicate or erroneous accounts cause payments to be drawn from the wrong record.
redFlags: Attempts to delete closed accounts with history

scr_cash_bank_account_information_page.purpose: The bank account record page holding bank details, GL account, entity restrictions, check settings, electronic payment and positive pay configuration.
scr_cash_bank_account_information_page.outcome: All settings governing how one bank account is used are defined in one place.
scr_cash_bank_account_information_page.rootCause: Positive pay, ACH origination and check printing all depend on bank account settings; errors here cause payments to be rejected or unprotected.
scr_cash_bank_account_information_page.ifSkipped: Positive pay not set up, leaving the account exposed to check fraud.
gaap: UCC 4-406 — customer duty and bank liability for fraud
redFlags: Positive pay disabled on accounts issuing checks

scr_cash_printing_wiring_instructions_fo.purpose: Prints wiring instructions for a bank account to give to parties sending funds — owners funding capital calls, lenders releasing reserve draws, insurance carriers paying claims.
scr_cash_printing_wiring_instructions_fo.outcome: Inbound wires go to the correct account.
scr_cash_printing_wiring_instructions_fo.rootCause: Wire fraud schemes impersonate property managers and send fake instructions. Official instructions generated from the system, sent through verified channels, reduce misdirected funds.
scr_cash_printing_wiring_instructions_fo.ifSkipped: Funds are wired to wrong or fraudulent accounts.
redFlags: Wiring instructions sent by unverified email

scr_cash_restricting_a_bank_account_to_o.purpose: Limits a bank account so only selected entities or locations can use it for payments and deposits.
scr_cash_restricting_a_bank_account_to_o.outcome: Cash usage is confined to the owners and properties the account belongs to.
scr_cash_restricting_a_bank_account_to_o.rootCause: Pooled and shared accounts are common in management companies, but each must be limited to its intended entities to avoid commingling owner funds.
scr_cash_restricting_a_bank_account_to_o.ifSkipped: Commingling of owner funds and unexpected intercompany balances.
gaap: Management agreement — no commingling of owner funds
State real estate broker trust rules
redFlags: Trust accounts available to all entities

scr_cash_credit_card_accounts_list.purpose: Lists corporate credit card accounts used by property staff, with their liability GL accounts and cardholders.
scr_cash_credit_card_accounts_list.outcome: An inventory of cards so each statement can be reconciled and charges coded to properties.
scr_cash_credit_card_accounts_list.rootCause: Site teams use cards for small purchases outside the PO process. Every card is a spending channel that must be reconciled and approved monthly.
scr_cash_credit_card_accounts_list.ifSkipped: Card statements go unreconciled and personal or unapproved charges are paid.
redFlags: Cards assigned to terminated employees

scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_account.purpose: Sets up a credit card account with ID, last four digits, issuer and liability GL account so card charges can be recorded and paid.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_account.outcome: Card charges post to the right liability and can be reconciled to the issuer's statement.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_account.rootCause: Card liabilities must be tracked separately from vendor A/P so statement balances can be reconciled and paid on time.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_account.ifSkipped: Card charges are recorded ad hoc and the card liability is unreconciled.
redFlags: Card accounts mapped to A/P rather than a card liability

scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_credit_car.purpose: Reviews or updates a card account's details, while locked fields (ID, last four digits) protect the link to posted transactions.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_credit_car.outcome: Card account details stay current without breaking transaction history.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_credit_car.rootCause: Card reissues and GL changes happen; locking identifiers prevents altering historical records.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_credit_car.ifSkipped: Card changes are not reflected and statements fail to reconcile.
redFlags: GL mapping changes mid-period

scr_cash_inactivating_or_deleting_a_cred.purpose: Inactivates a card account when a card is cancelled (preserving history) or deletes one created in error.
scr_cash_inactivating_or_deleting_a_cred.outcome: Cancelled cards cannot be used for new charges, while history remains.
scr_cash_inactivating_or_deleting_a_cred.rootCause: Cards of terminated employees must be shut off promptly to prevent unauthorized charges.
scr_cash_inactivating_or_deleting_a_cred.ifSkipped: Charges continue on cards that should be closed.
redFlags: Inactive cards with new charges

scr_cash_credit_card_account_page.purpose: Card account record page for adding, viewing and editing card details and GL mapping.
scr_cash_credit_card_account_page.outcome: A complete card record supporting reconciliation and payment.
scr_cash_credit_card_account_page.rootCause: Accurate card records are the basis of monthly card reconciliations and cardholder accountability.
scr_cash_credit_card_account_page.ifSkipped: Card reconciliation lacks a reliable master record.
redFlags: Cards with no assigned cardholder

scr_cash_periodic_tasks.purpose: Periodic Tasks section covering the recurring cash activities: deposits, funds transfers, manual payments, other receipts, available cash, holdbacks, payment files, positive pay and reconciliations.
scr_cash_periodic_tasks.outcome: A defined set of recurring cash activities performed on schedule.
scr_cash_periodic_tasks.rootCause: Cash tasks are recurring and deadline-driven (daily deposits, bank cut-offs, monthly recs). Grouping them supports a daily and monthly routine.
scr_cash_periodic_tasks.ifSkipped: Recurring cash tasks are missed, causing rec breaks and payment delays.
redFlags: Deposits not recorded daily

scr_cash_deposits.purpose: Explains deposits: grouping multiple payments (resident checks, money orders) into one deposit that matches what the bank shows on the statement.
scr_cash_deposits.outcome: Deposit records that mirror bank deposit lines one to one.
scr_cash_deposits.rootCause: Banks show deposits as totals; grouping receipts the same way makes the bank reconciliation match line for line.
scr_cash_deposits.ifSkipped: Bank recs require matching many small receipts to one deposit, and errors hide inside the totals.
redFlags: Deposits not matching deposit slips

scr_cash_deposits_workflow.purpose: Diagram of the deposits workflow: payment received into undeposited funds, grouped into a deposit, deposited at the bank, and matched in reconciliation.
scr_cash_deposits_workflow.outcome: Users understand where each receipt sits between collection and the bank.
scr_cash_deposits_workflow.rootCause: Receipts pass through several states; knowing the flow helps trace missing deposits, a common sign of cash misappropriation at the site.
scr_cash_deposits_workflow.ifSkipped: Missing deposits are not traced back to the receipts they came from.
redFlags: Receipts in undeposited funds for more than a few days

scr_cash_undeposited_funds_accounts.purpose: Configures the undeposited funds account in A/R that holds checks and cash received but not yet deposited.
scr_cash_undeposited_funds_accounts.outcome: A holding account whose balance shows receipts awaiting deposit.
scr_cash_undeposited_funds_accounts.rootCause: Receipts and deposits happen at different times. An undeposited funds account makes the gap visible so aged, undeposited receipts can be investigated.
scr_cash_undeposited_funds_accounts.ifSkipped: Receipts post straight to cash, hiding undeposited items and making the bank rec harder.
redFlags: Undeposited funds account not configured

scr_cash_deposits_list.purpose: Lists every deposit recorded through Cash Management with date, bank account, amount and status, for review, printing and reversal.
scr_cash_deposits_list.outcome: The book-side deposit register used to match against bank statement credits.
scr_cash_deposits_list.rootCause: Deposits in transit at month-end must be listed individually on the bank rec. The deposit list is where those items come from and where missing or duplicated deposits are spotted.
scr_cash_deposits_list.ifSkipped: Deposits in transit cannot be supported and missing site deposits (a key fraud red flag) go unnoticed.
redFlags: Deposits recorded but not cleared at the bank after several days

scr_cash_viewing_and_verifying_deposits.purpose: Opens a deposit to verify its payments and total against the deposit slip and bank credit.
scr_cash_viewing_and_verifying_deposits.outcome: Deposit errors (missing checks, wrong amounts) are caught before the bank rec.
scr_cash_viewing_and_verifying_deposits.rootCause: Deposit discrepancies at the site are an early fraud indicator and a common source of rec breaks.
redFlags: Deposit totals different from bank credits

scr_cash_printing_deposit_details.purpose: Prints the detail of a deposit — each payment, payer, check number and amount — to accompany the physical deposit or to support a deposit line on the bank reconciliation.
scr_cash_printing_deposit_details.outcome: A document proving which resident payments made up each bank deposit.
scr_cash_printing_deposit_details.rootCause: When a resident claims they paid and the ledger disagrees, or an auditor tests cash receipts, the deposit detail is the evidence connecting individual payments to the bank credit.
scr_cash_printing_deposit_details.ifSkipped: Resident payment disputes and audit samples cannot be resolved from bank records alone, since the bank shows only deposit totals.
gaap: AU-C 500 — audit evidence for cash receipts
redFlags: Deposit detail totals not equal to the bank credit

scr_cash_reversing_deposits.purpose: Explains that deposits cannot be deleted — only reversed — to keep an audit trail of cash activity.
scr_cash_reversing_deposits.outcome: Deposit corrections always leave a visible trail.
scr_cash_reversing_deposits.rootCause: Deleting deposits would allow cash records to be altered invisibly, a classic concealment method. Reversal preserves evidence.
scr_cash_reversing_deposits.ifSkipped: Deposit history could be altered without trace.
redFlags: Frequent deposit reversals at one property

scr_cash_reversing_a_deposit.purpose: Reverses a whole deposit (recorded to the wrong bank account or date), creating an offsetting line so the payments return to undeposited funds for re-deposit.
scr_cash_reversing_a_deposit.outcome: The erroneous deposit is cancelled and the payments can be deposited correctly.
scr_cash_reversing_a_deposit.rootCause: Deposits recorded to the wrong account break two bank recs. Reversal moves payments back without losing history.
scr_cash_reversing_a_deposit.ifSkipped: Deposits stay in the wrong account and both recs break.
redFlags: Reversal dated in a reconciled period

scr_cash_reversing_a_payment_in_a_deposi.purpose: Reverses one payment within a deposit — typically a resident check returned NSF — without reversing the whole deposit.
scr_cash_reversing_a_payment_in_a_deposi.outcome: The bounced payment is reinstated on the resident's account while the rest of the deposit stays intact.
scr_cash_reversing_a_payment_in_a_deposi.rootCause: NSF returns affect individual payments. Reversing only that payment keeps the deposit matched to the bank and re-opens the resident's balance for collection and NSF fees.
scr_cash_reversing_a_payment_in_a_deposi.ifSkipped: Bounced payments remain credited; A/R and cash are overstated.
redFlags: NSF items reversed without charging NSF fees per lease

scr_cash_deposit_page.purpose: The page used to record a bank deposit: choose the bank account and deposit date, then select the undeposited resident and other payments included in the physical or remote deposit.
scr_cash_deposit_page.outcome: A deposit record whose total matches the deposit slip and the bank credit line, moving receipts from Undeposited Funds to cash.
scr_cash_deposit_page.rootCause: The bank credits one total per deposit. Recording deposits exactly as they were made (same date, same checks) is what lets the bank rec match one book line to one bank line.
scr_cash_deposit_page.ifSkipped: Receipts sit in Undeposited Funds, cash is understated, and deposits must be matched to the bank by guesswork.
redFlags: Deposit date different from the bank credit date
Security deposits included in operating deposits

scr_cash_funds_transfer.purpose: Explains funds transfers — moving money between two cash accounts the company controls — as distinct from payments to third parties.
scr_cash_funds_transfer.outcome: Internal cash movements are recorded on both sides consistently.
scr_cash_funds_transfer.rootCause: Transfers are not income or expense, but they affect two bank recs. A dedicated transaction type ensures both sides are recorded together.
scr_cash_funds_transfer.ifSkipped: One-sided transfer entries break bank recs.
redFlags: Transfers recorded via JE

scr_cash_funds_transfer_list.purpose: Lists all recorded funds transfers — from account, to account, amount, date — for review, bank matching and reversal.
scr_cash_funds_transfer_list.outcome: A register of internal cash movements that should appear as matching debits and credits on two bank statements.
scr_cash_funds_transfer_list.rootCause: Each transfer must clear on both statements. The list is where accountants confirm both legs cleared and spot one-sided transfers.
scr_cash_funds_transfer_list.ifSkipped: One-sided transfers linger as reconciling items on two bank recs.
redFlags: Transfers cleared in one account but not the other

scr_cash_importing_funds_transfers.purpose: Imports many funds transfers from a template — e.g., daily sweeps for dozens of properties from the bank's sweep report.
scr_cash_importing_funds_transfers.outcome: High-volume transfers recorded quickly and consistently.
scr_cash_importing_funds_transfers.rootCause: Sweep structures generate a transfer per property per day; manual entry is impractical.
scr_cash_importing_funds_transfers.ifSkipped: Sweeps are recorded late or netted monthly, obscuring errors.
redFlags: Import totals not matching the bank sweep report

scr_cash_reversing_a_funds_transfer.purpose: Reverses a funds transfer that was recorded incorrectly, since transfers cannot be edited or voided.
scr_cash_reversing_a_funds_transfer.outcome: The wrong transfer is cancelled with an audit trail, and a correct one can be entered.
scr_cash_reversing_a_funds_transfer.rootCause: Locking transfers against edits preserves cash audit trails; reversal is the controlled correction path.
scr_cash_reversing_a_funds_transfer.ifSkipped: Wrong transfers remain and both bank recs break.
redFlags: Reversals without a replacement entry

scr_cash_funds_transfer_page.purpose: Page to record a transfer: from account, to account, amount, date and memo, with intercompany entries generated when entities differ.
scr_cash_funds_transfer_page.outcome: A balanced transfer that updates both cash accounts and any Due To/Due From.
scr_cash_funds_transfer_page.rootCause: Cross-entity transfers need intercompany entries to keep each entity balanced; the page generates them automatically.
scr_cash_funds_transfer_page.ifSkipped: Entities become unbalanced after cross-entity transfers.
redFlags: Cross-owner transfers without authorization

scr_cash_bulk_funds_transfer_page.purpose: Transfers funds from one account to many accounts in one action — e.g., funding several property operating accounts from an owner's concentration account after a capital call.
scr_cash_bulk_funds_transfer_page.outcome: Multi-property funding recorded in one step with consistent dates.
scr_cash_bulk_funds_transfer_page.rootCause: Owner funding and payroll funding often go from one account to many; bulk entry prevents missing properties.
scr_cash_bulk_funds_transfer_page.ifSkipped: Some properties' funding is not recorded, breaking their recs.
redFlags: Bulk totals not matching the bank's outgoing transfer

scr_cash_transferring_funds_in_bulk.purpose: Procedure for a bulk funds transfer: choose the source account (e.g., owner concentration account), add each destination property account and amount, and save as one transaction set.
scr_cash_transferring_funds_in_bulk.outcome: Owner or payroll funding to many properties is recorded in one step, matching the bank's outgoing transfers.
scr_cash_transferring_funds_in_bulk.rootCause: Owner funding after a capital call and payroll pre-funding go from one account to many. Entering them one at a time risks missing a property or keying a wrong amount.
scr_cash_transferring_funds_in_bulk.ifSkipped: Some property accounts show unexplained deposits on their recs and the source account shows an unexplained withdrawal total.
redFlags: Bulk total different from the bank's outgoing total

scr_cash_manual_payments.purpose: Section on recording and managing manual payments — payments made outside the normal A/P check run (wires, handwritten checks, online bill pay).
scr_cash_manual_payments.outcome: Off-cycle payments are captured in A/P and cash.
scr_cash_manual_payments.rootCause: Urgent payments (tax bills, utility shutoffs, insurance premiums) bypass the check run. Unless recorded, vendors look unpaid and cash does not reconcile.
redFlags: High volume of manual payments
